messages:
maya: Heads-up — after yesterday's kernel-selector flip to v2.14 on pool-3 we see p99 tail spikes under sustained high concurrency. Looks correlated with KV cache evictions (evict rate jumped ~3x). Posting quick notes + flame snippet.
sam: Which model + microbatch config? numbers?
maya: model: opt-6.7b-quant, target-slo=150ms, observed p95 ~ 98ms, p99 jumped to 520ms during bursts at ~620 concurrent reqs. KV evict rate log:
```
[2026-03-16T21:02:11Z] kv_evict: rate=0.32/s window=120s
[2026-03-16T21:02:11Z] kv_misses: 0.18/s
[2026-03-16T21:02:11Z] mb_window_ms=10 kernels=v2.14
```
maya: flame (very small ASCII excerpt):
```
-- serve_loop
   -- microbatch_assemble
      -- kv_fetch (p99 spike)
         -- memcpy
         -- kernel_dispatch
```
sam: microbatch window is 10ms right? that's larger than usual for this model distribution.
drew: my hunch: v2.14's kernel probes cause slightly higher per-token memory churn which under high concurrency increases KV pressure -> more evictions -> increased p99 due to remote reloads. Two levers: shrink microbatch window OR increase kv_capacity threshold.
alex: Another angle: kernel selection fallback path in v2.14 routes some attention patterns to a slower kernel if seq_len>256. If KV restarts align with those fallbacks, we get amplified tails. Might be a kernel/kv interaction.
maya: Quick A/B I ran for 10min each on pool-3 canary:
A (v2.14, mb=10ms): p95=102ms p99=480ms evict_rate=0.31/s
B (v2.13, mb=10ms): p95=100ms p99=160ms evict_rate=0.09/s
C (v2.14, mb=6ms): p95=99ms p99=170ms evict_rate=0.08/s
So shrinking microbatch to 6ms basically recovers tail but costs ~4% throughput.
sam: good data. So tradeoff is microbatch sizing vs throughput. We want an automated knob: adaptive mb that tightens under kv_pressure.
perf-bot: [alert] perf/regression: p99 spike detected on pool-3 after deploy (commit: 9f3b2a) dashboard: https://perf.redwood/compare/9f3b2a
alex: I'll add a KV pressure signal to the routing decision: if evict_rate>0.2/s then reduce batch window for that shard to 6ms and pin kernel to v2.13 as fallback. Also add short cooldown so we don't thrash.
drew: also worth adding a quick microbenchmark: simulate high-concurrency random keys and measure eviction heatmap vs mb. I can run this tonight.
maya: run commands I used:
```
# perf harness
./tools/rtm-run --pool pool-3 --model opt-6.7b --concurrency 620 --duration 600 --mb-window 10 --profile out_a.pb
./tools/rtm-run --pool pool-3 --model opt-6.7b --concurrency 620 --duration 600 --mb-window 6  --profile out_b.pb
```
maya: logs and profiles uploaded to /s3/perf/pool3/1978765432/
sam: schedule for canary revert + adaptive-mb tweak this morning? I can own the rollout.
maya: Yes, please. If canary looks good let's keep v2.13 pinned for pool-3 until we root-cause kernel mem churn. Thanks all :thumbsup:
perf-bot: deploybot: started canary rollback (job: rollback/pool-3/1978765432)
alex: I'll open a short RFC to add kv_eviction metric to trace spans and a heuristic for adaptive batching. small PR incoming.
